title: The Fruit of the Spirit
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: The fruit of the Spirit is the Christlike character the Holy Spirit produces in believers. This fruit is not self-made virtue, but the visible evidence of the Spirit’s life and work over time.
summary: The fruit of the Spirit is the Christlike character the Holy Spirit produces in believers. This fruit is not self-made virtue, but the visible evidence of the Spirit’s life and work over time.
christFocus: The Spirit forms the character of Christ in God’s people. The fruit of the Spirit reflects the love, purity, gentleness, faithfulness, and self-control seen perfectly in Jesus.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
The Spirit produces fruit in believers that the flesh cannot produce. Love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness, and self-control grow from the Spirit’s life within God’s people.

This fruit is connected to abiding in Christ. Branches do not bear fruit by detaching from the vine. Believers bear fruit as they remain dependent on Christ, receive His Word, and walk by the Spirit.

Fruit is different from outward performance. A person can appear religious, gifted, or active while lacking Christlike character. The Spirit’s fruit reaches the heart, speech, desires, relationships, and conduct.

The growth of fruit is often gradual. Believers may still struggle, but the Spirit patiently forms real character that glorifies God and blesses others.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Many people measure spirituality by visibility, emotion, knowledge, or gifting. Scripture teaches believers to look for fruit. The Spirit’s work is seen not only in what people do publicly, but in who they are becoming before God.

This doctrine gives hope to ordinary believers. Spiritual growth may feel slow, but the Spirit is able to produce lasting character that human effort alone cannot create.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Ask the Spirit to grow His fruit in you. Do not settle for outward religion while neglecting character. Abide in Christ, confess the works of the flesh, practice obedience, and look for growth in love, patience, gentleness, faithfulness, and self-control in daily life.
